---
title: "Paradigm Completion"
date: 2026-05-01
description: "A discussion of the paradigm completion problem in coding agents and how it differs from natural language understanding."
tags: [coding agents, language models, paradigm completion]
---

Paradigm completion is the problem of filling in all the forms of a morphological paradigm given the base form. 

e.g.: walk/walks/walked/walking

|Person|Base Form|Present|Past|Present Participle|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|I|walk|walks|walked|walking|
|You|walk|walk|walked|walking|
|He/She/It|walk|walks|walked|walking|
|We|walk|walk|walked|walking|
|You (plural)|walk|walk|walked|walking|
|They|walk|walk|walked|walking|

In english this is a minor problem because the paradigm is relatively simple and regular.

Latin from which many of the romance languages are derived has a much more complex paradigm 

[Macedo, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CONIUGATIO.png)

In hebrew this is a much more significant problem because the paradigm is much more complex and irregular. For example, the verb "to write" has 46 different forms in the present tense alone, and there are many irregular verbs that do not follow the standard patterns.

for the verb "to write" in hebrew we have the following paradigms:

However in hebrew where the Academy of the Hebrew Language has identified 46 different paradigms, this is a much more significant problem. And in particular for neolegisms which the academy introduces every year.
